input.quote: 12.3.2 Minimum Requirements. Commencing as of the start of the Clinical Trials and thereafter, during the Term (or longer if otherwise stated below), at a minimum, each Party will maintain the following types of insurance coverage at a minimum level that is the greater of (a) the highest minimum level required by Applicable Law in the countries in which the Clinical Trials and other obligations hereunder are being performed or (b) the following (to the extent different).
input.rationale: An insurance regime is present and substantially exceeds the rule's structural expectations, so no redline is warranted. § 12.3.1–12.3.2 obliges each Party (including SFJ) to carry commercial general liability, umbrella excess liability, clinical trials liability and, for subcontractors providing professional services, professional liability insurance, in each case at the greater of the stated limits or the highest limit required by Applicable Law (which picks up statutory workers' compensation), with insurers rated at least "A-" A.M. Best and policies primary and non-contributing. Certificates of insurance are supplied on written request pre-signing and annually (§ 12.3.1), advance written notice is required on cancellation, non-renewal or material change, and each Party must ensure subcontractors and Permitted Third Parties are insured before continuing work (§ 12.3.2). § 12.3.3 adds additional-insured status for the other Party on clinical trial liability cover, and § 12.3.4 allocates product liability cover with the other Party named as additional insured. § 12.3.2 also confirms insurance does not cap either Party's liability. Two minor sub-elements fall short of the preferred wording and are noted rather than flagged: (i) there is no dedicated cyber/privacy liability line, though this is a clinical development funding arrangement rather than a hosting or data-processing engagement, and clinical trial and professional liability cover carries the relevant risk; and (ii) the numeric limits are redacted ([***]) in our copy, so the USD thresholds cannot be independently verified — we should confirm the unredacted figures against the preferred limits in diligence. The obligations are mutual and largely protective of us, so flagging them would work against our interest.
